subject.title: fix: allow trusted host-read html after outbound staging

question: Should outbound-staged generated HTML be accepted for host-read delivery when the staged file has matching SQLite provenance and content digest?
rationale: The code path is mechanically reviewable, but deciding whether this persisted provenance lifecycle is an acceptable local HTML trust expansion requires maintainer/security intent.

options.title: Accept content-bound provenance
options.body: Land the PR once exact-head checks and mergeability are current, treating sha256/size-backed SQLite provenance as the approved lifecycle for staged generated HTML.

options.title: Require a narrower trust model
options.body: Ask for a revision that keeps the trust signal more internal or changes the provenance lifecycle before merge.

options.title: Reject outbound HTML trust expansion
options.body: Leave temp-root-only trusted HTML behavior in place and solve the linked Telegram delivery failure through a different delivery path.

recommendation.title: Accept content-bound provenance
recommendation.body: Land the PR once exact-head checks and mergeability are current, treating sha256/size-backed SQLite provenance as the approved lifecycle for staged generated HTML.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the trusted generated HTML host-read seam and are the strongest history-backed owner for accepting or rejecting this boundary.
